subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight implement single active-target suppression for configured bots/agents, including how role mentions, quoted text, and plain-text agent-name delegation participate?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing these rules can intentionally suppress traffic that existing multi-agent Discord setups currently receive through default-owner or binding routes.

options.title: Adopt active-target suppression
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target selection before default routing, allow explicit current-bot mentions, and suppress other configured targets with focused tests and live Discord proof.

options.title: Split native precedence first
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13487 own native mention/reply/default-owner precedence while this issue tracks quoted-text, role, and bot-authored residual cases.

options.title: Defer fuzzy signals
options.body: Fix only native Discord metadata now and leave role-label and plain-text delegation semantics to separate product decisions.

recommendation.title: Adopt active-target suppression
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target selection before default routing, allow explicit current-bot mentions, and suppress other configured targets with focused tests and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent mention/routing history and prior cluster comments point to steipete as the strongest available decision owner.
